title: Effect of Heat Treatment on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Corrosion Resistance of ZK60 Alloy Produced via Wire-Based Electron-Beam Additive Manufacturing
content: Light-weight ZK60 magnesium alloy was successfully fabricated by a wire-feed electron beam additive manufacturing (EBAM). Beneficial effects of the «T4» heat treat-ment (515 °C, 2 h) on its microstructure, phase composition, texture, microhardness, and corrosion resistance were revealed. Vacuum-assisted welding of 2-mm ZK60 wire resulted in a non-monotonic zinc evaporation along the wall’s height and segregation of Zn–Zr phases along the interlayer boundaries, as well as MgZn2 precipitations at the grain boundaries. Proposed heat treatment promoted a homogenization of the micro-structure, dissolution of the eutectic MgZn2 network and enrichment of the α-Mg phase with Zn. Additionally, the mean sizes of coherent scattering domains increased from ~56 nm to 80 nm, while the lattice distortions reduced down to 0.04 %, according to the XRD analysis. The as-printed alloy was found to exhibit the poorest corrosion re-sistance in marine solution (3.5 wt. % NaCl) in comparison with the reference (as-cast) alloy. In this scope, the heat-treated alloy possessed the largest value of polarization resistance (Rp ~ 180 Ω·cm²) and the lowest corrosion current, reaching ~2 ·10⁻⁵ A/cm2. Homogenization annealing (T4) was considered to be an effective post-processing technique for improving corrosion characteristics of the EBAMed ZK60-type materials, but it is not suitable for the load-bearing applications.
